title: Claude Code's 2026 Architecture: Layers, Nested Subagents & Marketplace
content:
## Overview

Through 2026, Claude Code evolved from a single agentic loop into a **layered agentic system**: memory, hooks, skills, subagents, plugins, and MCP each own a distinct part of the model's behavior. Alongside that architectural shift, June–August 2026 brought hierarchical subagents, a community plugin marketplace, fallback model chains, per-agent cost attribution, and cross-session notifications. This page covers what changed since the original Claude Code overview.

---

## The Six-Layer Model

Each layer answers a different question about what the model can see or do:

| Layer | Owns |
|---|---|
| **CLAUDE.md** | Stable context — the repo's "constitution": conventions, commands, architecture notes read every session |
| **Output styles** | Response behavior — tone, verbosity, format defaults |
| **Skills** | Reusable procedures — folder-based instruction packs (a `SKILL.md` plus optional helper scripts/assets) loaded on demand when the task matches |
| **Slash commands** | Explicit, user-triggered workflows |
| **Hooks** | Deterministic lifecycle policy — things that must happen regardless of what the agent decides (e.g., always run a linter after an edit) |
| **Subagents** | Isolated work — a bounded task with its own context window, prompt, and tool permissions |
| **Plugins** | Distribution — bundles of the above primitives (skills, hooks, commands, agents) as one installable unit |
| **MCP** | External tools, resources, prompts, and durable system boundaries |

The practical upshot: when deciding how to encode a new behavior, the question isn't "prompt or code" but which layer fits — a one-off instruction is a skill, a must-always-happen check is a hook, an isolated multi-step task is a subagent, and a shareable bundle of all three is a plugin.

---

## Nested Subagents

Claude Code subagents can now spawn their own child subagents, **up to five levels deep** (an increase from the original three-level cap). A parent agent decomposes a large task, hands bounded pieces to children, and each child can further decompose its own piece — useful for operations spanning many modules or files where a flat fan-out isn't enough structure.

**Practical limits reported by early adopters:** token cost compounds quickly with depth (each level adds its own context overhead), so most production setups cap real-world usage at 2–3 levels even though 5 is technically supported, and reserve deeper nesting for genuinely hierarchical work (e.g., "audit every service" → "audit every module in this service" → "audit every file in this module").

---

## Community Plugin Marketplace

Claude Code now ships a searchable plugin marketplace, reachable via `/plugins search`. It surfaces community-built extensions — bundled skills, hooks, subagent definitions, and slash commands — for use cases like code review, security scanning, and documentation generation. Plugins are the distribution unit: installing one wires up all the primitives it bundles in a single step, rather than copying individual hook scripts or agent files by hand.

---

## Fallback Model Chains & Cost Controls

You can now configure a **fallback model chain** for a session or agent — if the primary model is rate-limited, degraded, or unavailable, Claude Code automatically retries with the next model in the chain instead of failing the turn. Combined with per-task cost budgets, this is aimed at solo developers and small teams who want resilience without building custom retry orchestration.

`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL` is a new environment variable that sets which model a *new* session starts on, independent of the fallback chain used mid-session.

---

## Per-Agent Cost Attribution

OpenTelemetry traces emitted by Claude Code now include a `model` attribute identifying which model handled each span. In a multi-level subagent hierarchy, this lets teams break down cost and latency **per agent, per task** — important once nested subagents mean a single top-level request can fan out into dozens of underlying model calls across different tiers (e.g., Haiku for cheap leaf tasks, Opus for the coordinating agent).

---

## Cross-Session Notifications & Collaboration

- **`notify_when_idle`**: a cross-session `SendMessage` mechanism — one Claude Code session can be notified when another session (potentially working on a related task) goes idle, useful for coordinating handoffs between parallel sessions.
- **`@`-mention across sessions**: typing `@` lets you reference and pull in another running Claude session directly, for lightweight collaboration between sessions without manually copying context.
- **GitLab merge request support**: the worktree view now supports GitLab MRs alongside GitHub PRs.
- **Runaway build protection**: new memory limits prevent build commands from exhausting container resources.

---

## Security & Platform Hardening

- **Stronger macOS sandbox protections** for local sessions.
- Improvements to **Remote Control**, **auto mode**, startup speed, and VS Code screen-reader support shipped through July–August 2026.

---

## Key Takeaways

- Claude Code's internals are now explicitly documented as **six layers** (memory, output styles, skills, commands, hooks, subagents/plugins, MCP) — pick the layer that matches the durability and triggering model you need, not just "prompt vs. code."
- **Nested subagents** go up to 5 levels deep, but token cost compounds with depth — most teams stay at 2–3 in practice.
- A **plugin marketplace** (`/plugins search`) makes community-built skill/hook/agent bundles installable in one step.
- **Fallback model chains** plus **per-agent cost attribution** (via OpenTelemetry `model` attributes) address resilience and cost visibility in multi-agent setups.
- Cross-session `notify_when_idle` and `@`-mention support lighter-weight collaboration between concurrent Claude Code sessions.
